Safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of MK-6194, an IL-2 mutein 
designed to selectively activate regulatory T cells: single ascending dose and 
multiple ascending dose trial data.

Scheid JF(1), Cunningham-Bussel K(1), Kim N(1), Agarwal S(1), Nieddu G(1), Cote 
J(1), Lemoine L(1), Decaesteker T(1), Mendez L(1), Paul E(1), Love-Gregory L(1), 
Contreras AV(1), Zhao X(1), Franco-Dilone L(1), Pang L(1), Baltus GA(1), 
Beaumont M(1), Shah K(1), Higginson-Scott N(2), Kis-Toth K(2), Otipoby KL(2), 
Viney JL(2), Sicard E(3), Rottey S(4), Sundy JS(2), Van Dyck K(1), Laethem T(1), 
Larson P(1), Sutradhar S(1), Wnek R(1), Bueters T(1), Lai E(1), Stoch SA(1), 
Iwamoto M(1), Robbins JA(1).

Author information:
(1)Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, United States.
(2)Pandion Therapeutics, Inc., a subsidiary of Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, 
United States.
(3)Altasciences, Montreal, QC, Canada.
(4)Universiteit Gent, Gent, Belgium.

MK-6194, an interleukin-2 mutein designed to selectively activate regulatory T 
cells (Tregs), was evaluated for safety, pharmacokinetics (PK), immunogenicity, 
and pharmacodynamics in healthy participants. In a single ascending dose trial 
(N = 56), participants received subcutaneous MK-6194 or placebo (3:1 ratio) 
across dose levels ranging from 1 to 10 mg. In a multiple ascending dose trial 
(N = 54), participants received subcutaneous MK-6194 or placebo (3:1 ratio) at 
dose levels ranging from 0.5 to 5 mg every 2 wk (total 3 doses) as well as 5 mg 
every 4 wk (total 2 doses). Baseline characteristics were comparable between 
trials, with participants mostly male with a mean age of 36 yr. There were no 
serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities. The most common adverse 
events were injection site erythema and eosinophil count elevations (with no 
indication of severe eosinophilia or eosinophilia-related organ damage). PK
